statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Mercantil Central (RMC) – Sede Electrónica, online application for 'Certificación Negativa de Denominación Social'
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be written in Spanish or in any co-official language of an Autonomous Community (Catalan, Basque, Galician). Foreign expressions must be transliterated into Latin alphabetic script. The legal form suffix 'Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada' or 'S.L.' is mandatory. The name must not be identical or phonetically/visually similar to an existing registered name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A negative name certificate is valid for 180 days from issuance. If the incorporation deed is not executed within this window, a new application with the same or revised name must be filed and the fee paid again. Upon rejection, the applicant may file a written administrative appeal with the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública within one month of the negative certificate, stating the grounds of objection and supporting registrability arguments; referral to a specialized registrar is possible and judicial review under the Ley 39/2015 administrative procedure is available at final instance.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or professional address is initially permissible for registration of an SL under Article 9 of the Ley de Sociedades de Capital, provided it is a genuine address for receipt of notifications and service of process. However, for ISIC 5820 (simulated social casino / virtual slots publishing) with commercial payment rails through Apple IAP and Google Play Billing, banks and payment providers require physical substance, local management presence, and a dedicated bookkeeping office. A purely virtual address is not acceptable for operating revenue flows or for obtaining a gaming-related merchant account, and tax authorities may challenge lack of economic substance for corporate tax and VAT purposes.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 65% probability of an unannounced physical inspection within the first 24 months of operation, rising to 85% if the registered office remains a virtual address without substantive local operations, personnel, or infrastructure.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Spain — Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010, de 2 de julio, Ley de Sociedades de Capital (LSC): Arts. 4 (minimum capital), 20-22 (formal constitution), 23 (articles of association content), 33 (legal personality upon registration), 62 (bank deposit certificate), 129-130 (participaciones), 209 and 221-233 (administrators); Ley 14/2013, de 27 de septiembre, de apoyo a los emprendedores: Arts. 4 bis and 15-16 (CIRCE/PAIT expeditious incorporation and 'sociedad de formación sucesiva'); Real Decreto 1784/1996 (Reglamento del Registro Mercantil); Ley 10/2010 (AML and beneficial-ownership declarations); Código de Comercio, Arts. 16-21.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Mercantil Central (denomination certification, Madrid) and Registro Mercantil Provincial competent for the registered office (e.g., Registro Mercantil de Madrid); online one-stop shop CIRCE (www.circe.es) operated with the Ventanilla Única de Creación de Empresas.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura pública de constitución (public deed granted before a Spanish Notary), filed as 'primera copia autorizada' for inscription in the Mercantile Registry; under the CIRCE route, a Documento Único Electrónico (DUE) and telematic notarial record replace the paper deed.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Statutory default: EUR 3,000 (approx. USD 3,250) minimum paid-up capital, fully subscribed and paid in cash at the execution of the deed (Arts. 4.1 and 62.1 LSC); each participacion has a nominal value of EUR 1.00. The deposit must be made in a Spanish bank account in the company's name and the bank's certificate of deposit is attached to the deed; no locked escrow is required by law, but the depositary bank may only release funds upon presentation of the deed, with return to founders permitted only under Art. 62.3 LSC if registration fails. Alternative: under Ley 14/2013 a 'sociedad de formación sucesiva' may be formed with capital below EUR 3,000, subject to statutory restrictions (no distributions, mandatory reserve, and the obligation to reach EUR 3,000 within 24 months).
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION — SOCIEDAD DE RESPONSABILIDAD LIMITADA [COMPANY NAME] ('the Company'), Madrid. The Sole Founder unanimously resolves: (1) the subscription of 3,000 participaciones, nominal value EUR 1.00 each (EUR 3,000), fully paid into a Spanish credit institution; (2) the adoption of the registered office at [Address], Madrid, within the Madrid Mercantile Registry's jurisdiction; (3) the appointment of [Name Surname] as Administrador Único (sole director) under Article 209 LSC, with full management and representation powers; (4) authorization to the director to execute the public deed, to obtain the NIF, and to effect all post-incorporation filings with the Mercantile Registry, tax authorities, and social security; (5) ratification of all acts performed in the Company's name during formation. Adopted unanimously.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Negative Name Certificate (Certificación de Denominación Social)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Central (RMC), Calle Buenos Aires 1-3, 28043 Madrid — online via the RMC telematic application (www.rmc.es) or through a Notary or gestor.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an online application listing up to five proposed company names in order of preference. The RMC searches the central registry database for identical or confusingly similar names and, if clear, issues a 'certificación negativa de denominación social' (negative name certificate). The certificate is sealed and valid for three months from issuance, renewable once for an additional three months; it must be presented to the Notary at the incorporation deed. The certificate must identify the applicant and the intended company type (SL).
required_dossiers: Completed RMC formal request (solicitud de certificación) with up to five proposed denominations
Copy of the petitioner's national ID (DNI/NIE) or passport
Statement of the intended corporate purpose in Spanish
Payment of the certificate fee (approx. EUR 30-40)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry rejects the application because the requested denomination coincides with an existing name or is prohibited (e.g., identity with official state bodies or offensive terms), the applicant re-submits immediately with the alternative candidate names; checking the RMC's public name database first avoids further rejections. There is no formal appeal because a fresh application may be filed at any time before the notarial deed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Provisional NIF and Capital Deposit at a Spanish Credit Institution
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) — Delegación de Gestión Tributaria (provisional NIF via Modelo 036); any Spanish bank supervised by the Banco de España for the capital deposit.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Where required by the bank, first obtain the provisional NIF by filing Modelo 036 (census declaration) in the name of the company 'en formación', which yields a provisional NIF ending in 'P'. Open a corporate account at a Spanish bank in the exact proposed company name, deposit the full subscribed capital (minimum EUR 3,000 under the general rule, or a lower amount if proceeding under the Ley 14/2013 'sociedad de formación sucesiva' regime), and request the 'certificado de depósito' evidencing the deposit and the bank's undertaking to release the funds only against the deed. The certificate must be addressed to the company and specify the depositors and amounts.
required_dossiers: Provisional NIF (if already granted) or completed Modelo 036 to apply for it
Valid negative name certificate
Passport/DNI/NIE of all founders and the future administrator
Draft Articles of Association (borrador de estatutos)
Bank account opening forms and AML/KYC documentation (Ley 10/2010)
Beneficial-ownership self-declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses to open the account invoking the AML risk typology of gaming-software publishing, provide a written compliance statement confirming that only simulated social-casino products without real-money stakes or prizes will be published; if AEAT declines the provisional NIF due to an incomplete Modelo 036, rectify and resubmit the form electronically; a bank's internal policy refusal can be cured by selecting another credit institution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the Public Deed of Incorporation before a Notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary (Notario) selected by the founders within the notarial district of the registered office, under the supervision of the Colegio Notarial; for the CIRCE route, notarization occurs through the integrated CIRCE telematic platform.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Attend the notarial appointment (or complete the CIRCE online procedure). The Notary verifies the identity and legal capacity of the founders, the lawfulness of the corporate purpose (which must expressly include the publishing of simulated social-casino and virtual-slots software with no real-money stakes or economic prizes), the registered office, share capital, participation structure, administration rule, and the remaining statutory content of Art. 23 LSC. The Notary records the subscription and payment of participaciones, uses the bank deposit certificate, assigns the provisional NIF where not previously obtained, and then authorizes the 'escritura pública de constitución'. A first authorized copy (primera copia autorizada) is issued for filing at the Mercantile Registry.
required_dossiers: Valid negative name certificate
Bank certificate of capital deposit
Draft Articles of Association aligned with Art. 23 LSC
Passports/DNI/NIE of all founding members
DNI/NIE of the appointed Administrador Único
AML beneficial-ownership declarations (Ley 10/2010 and Order EHA/114/2008)
Notarial fee payment (approx. EUR 350-500 under the notarial arancel)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Notary refuses to authorize the deed (e.g., unlawful statute clause, insufficient or improperly evidenced capital, or defective corporate purpose), the founders amend the draft and execute a new deed; if a founder is unavailable on the date, the deed may be executed through a notarial power of attorney (escritura de apoderamiento) or the appointment is rescheduled without loss of the name certificate validity.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Inscription in the Provincial Mercantile Registry (Registro Mercantil Provincial)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Provincial of the province of the registered office (e.g., Registro Mercantil de Madrid), Calle Príncipe de Vergara 80, Madrid; functioning under the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within two months from the date of the deed, submit the 'primera copia autorizada' of the deed together with the signature-matching sheet and the registry fee (arancel). The Registrar performs the legality review (calificación registral), verifying compliance with the LSC, the payment of capital, the legality of the corporate purpose (including the exclusion of real-money gambling to keep the activity outside Ley 13/2011), the registered office clause, and the administrator appointment. Upon approval, the company is inscribed and acquires legal personality (Art. 33 LSC). Request a certified registration certificate (certificación registral) for subsequent tax and operational filings.
required_dossiers: First authorized copy (primera copia autorizada) of the deed
Second copy marked for the Registry
Bank certificate of deposit
Provisional NIF certificate (if obtained)
Modelo 600 or AJD exemption certificate (formation and capital increases up to EUR 1,000,000 are exempt since Ley 4/2008)
Power of attorney if a representative files the documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar suspends or denies inscription through a 'nota de calificación' (e.g., statutory defect, capital payment irregularity, or inadequate corporate purpose clause), the founders cure the defect by filing supplementary documents before the Registrar; if the defect is in the deed itself, execute a rectification deed before the same Notary and re-present the corrected copy; if the Registrar maintains the refusal, an appeal (recurso gubernativo) lies to the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública within two months.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) — Sede Electrónica: https://sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es; customs administration integrated in the Departamento de Aduanas e Impuestos Especiales de la AEAT; national register: Censo de Obligados Tributarios.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1 – Incorporation: obtain provisional NIF (9-character fiscal identity, format X-1234567-X) for the SL at notarial signature through the notary; the provisional NIF is issued by AEAT. Step 2 – Definitive NIF: after registration in the Registro Mercantil of the corporate seat, file Form 030/036 for confirmation; definitive NIF must be obtained within six months of incorporation. Step 3 – Fiscal census enrollment: file Form 036 (Declaración censal de alta) electronically with an electronic certificate (DNIe/FNMT digital certificate, Cl@ve PIN, or authorized representative) for (i) Impuesto sobre Sociedades, (ii) IVA (título preliminar LIVA), (iii) employee withholdings (IRPF), and (iv) EORI number (customs) if physical exports are contemplated. Step 4 – Non-resident foreign entities without Spanish permanent establishment must file Form 034 (Censo de no establecidos) and appoint a VAT fiscal representative when required (mandatory for non-EU operators without an EU establishment performing B2C electronic supplies in Spain); a valid NIF-IE/NIE is obtained concurrent with the appointment. Step 5 – Post-registration: quarterly/annual returns (Form 303/390, Form 200, Form 349, Form 115/123/111 withholdings) accessible through the AEAT Sede Electrónica.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation: An SL is a unitary legal person with unlimited Spanish tax liability (worldwide income) under Ley 27/2014 (LIS); it is not eligible for pass-through/attribution treatment, unlike civil partnerships (sociedades civiles) or EIGs. Territorial scope: Spanish residence is determined primarily by place of incorporation; no territorial quarantine for foreign-source income except treaty-compliant tax credits. The SL is also a VAT taxable person (LIVA) automatically upon registration in the census, irrespective of profit motive.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Spain has no U.S.-style check-the-box election. Elective mechanisms relevant to cross-border groups include: (1) Consolidated tax group election under Art. 56–64 LIS, requiring 75% direct/indirect ownership and unanimous consent; group taxation centralizes the common rate offset; (2) OSS (One-Stop-Shop) election for intra-EU B2C electronically supplied services and distance sales (Form 036/C homologation), with quarterly filing; (3) election to file provisional tax loss carry-back refunds limited by statutory caps; (4) election of the reduced Corporate Income Tax rules for newly created entities (15% on first EUR 300,000 of basis) is statutory but must be exercised in the annual return; (5) hybrid mismatch rules under LIS Art. 15 quáter/15 quinquies (ATAD 1&2) apply automatically without opt-out; taxpayers may, however, elect the audit and transfer-pricing documentation regimes to pre-empt challenge. For customs/imports: AEO (Authorized Economic Operator) certification election provides simplifications and duty deferrals.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España (Bank of Spain), operating within the European System of Central Banks, together with the Spanish Ministry of Economy and Finance for foreign-investment statistical registration under Law 19/2003 on Capital Movements.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Spain has full current and capital account convertibility as a eurozone member. There are no exchange-control licences, no prior conversion requirements, and no quantitative restrictions on profit remittance or dividend distributions to non-resident shareholders. Dividends are freely transferable in EUR or any convertible currency; commercial withholding tax and treaty relief are separate corporate tax matters, not convertibility constraints. Only post-transaction statistical declarations and anti-money-laundering documentation obligations apply.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Not applicable. Spain imposes no mandatory surrender period, no minimum conversion ratio, and no obligation to repatriate export proceeds. Export receivables may be held in foreign currency or converted at market rates. Treasury must still satisfy Council Regulation (EU) 2015/847 transfer-of-funds transparency, Law 10/2010 AML/KYC obligations, and the Spanish Balance-of-Payments statistical reporting requirements when applicable.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High for EEA-licensed electronic money institutions passporting into Spain under PSD2; Low to Medium for offshore non-EEA digital EMIs. An offshore EMI cannot lawfully provide payment accounts or money transmission services into Spain without an EU/EEA authorisation or a licensed EU partner. Most EMIs classify social casino and virtual in-game currency flows as high-risk commercial verticals and may decline onboarding unless the corporate structure demonstrates no real-money pay-outs, no withdrawal facility, no secondary trading of virtual credits, and exclusive reliance on Apple IAP or Google Play Billing as the merchant settlement channel.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Directors are not statutorily required to appear physically at the bank, but a Spanish notarial power of attorney or notarised board resolution appointing local signatories is commonly required for account opening. Tier 1 banks will typically require enhanced due diligence interviews for non-resident directors and ultimate beneficial owners, conducted either in person at a Spanish branch or through an approved secure video identity process. For a Spanish SL in the social casino software vertical, the bank may require physical presence or apostilled certified copies of passports, corporate registry extracts, UBO declarations, evidence of source of funds, and a legal opinion confirming the absence of real-money gambling authorisation requirements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opacity in the ultimate beneficial ownership chain, especially with non-resident corporate shareholders.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full corporate chain documents from jurisdiction of incorporation to ultimate individuals; notarised Spanish SL deed and Registro Mercantil certificate; UBO declaration under Law 10/2010; apostilled passports; source of wealth and source of funds statements; tax residence certificates of shareholders.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Classification of the social casino product as gambling or unlicensed gaming, triggering higher AML and reputational risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Spanish gaming-law counsel legal opinion confirming no real-money gambling and no statutory licence requirement; product audit and game mechanics documentation showing no cash-out, no convertible virtual currency, and no secondary market; final user terms and conditions prohibiting sale or transfer of virtual chips; payment rail evidence tied to Apple IAP and Google Play Billing.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of non-resident directors or shareholders appearing on EU or international sanction/PEП lists or residency in high-risk third countries.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Clear negative sanctions screening; passport and NIE certificates; professional or bank reference letters; CV showing operational management; source of funds from regulated banking accounts; declaration of no politically exposed persons without proper senior-management approval.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk digital goods with potential fraud, refund abuse, or chargeback exposure through app-store purchasing.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed payment-process flow showing Apple/Google as merchants of record; app-store developer account standing; consumer refund policy; fraud, velocity, and platform abuse monitoring procedures; monthly reconciliation records between app-store financial reports, backend telemetry, and treasury settlements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ambiguity of the initial capital injection and inability to evidence clean source of corporate funds.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised capital contribution deed; bank statements from contributing shareholder; tax filing of the shareholder for the contribution; accounting of the SL showing share capital and share premium; Spanish foreign-investment statistical declaration where applicable; board resolution approving capital injection.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity capital should be remitted using SEPA Credit Transfer for EUR from an EEA account or SWIFT MT103 for non-EEA or non-EUR flows, with the payment reference identifying direct investment or equity capital contribution. The SL should segregate equity capital flows from operational app-store revenue, maintain the Spanish notarial capital increase or incorporation deed, retain the contributing shareholder's bank statements and identity/KYC evidence, and complete any applicable post-transaction Spanish foreign-investment registration with the Ministry of Economy and Finance. No prior exchange-control authorisation is required because Spain guarantees free capital movement.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use SEPA Credit Transfer in EUR for counterparties within the SEPA zone; use SWIFT MT103 for non-EEA or non-EUR trade settlements; use commercial letters of credit issued under UCP600 for significant import or licensing commitments; and use MT202 covers for interbank liquidity. All disbursements must be linked to executed contracts, commercial invoices, treasury approval records, and transfer-pricing documentation. Apple IAP and Google Play net-revenue remittances are settled through each platform's B2B/treasury flow, which must be reconciled against the monthly financial reports generated by the app-store console.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright EUR/FX forwards for G10 and Latin American currencies
FX swaps and rollover operations executed through the interbank forward market
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for restricted or less liquid emerging-market currencies, executed under ISDA with an EU-authorised bank
Cross-currency swaps for medium-term trade or financing exposures
Vanilla European-style currency options for hedging under a board-approved treasury policy
All instruments must be documented under ISDA/EMIR, cleared or reported as applicable, and limited to genuine commercial exposure without speculative uncovered positions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 25 calendar days following the expiry of 6 months after the fiscal year close; for a calendar-year entity this falls on 1–25 July of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing surcharge: 5% plus 1% per calendar month of delay (capped at 12 months); plus late-payment interest of 3.75% for 2024; penalties of 50%–150% of tax assessed for incorrect or omitted declarations; no administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts (Cuentas Anuales: balance sheet, profit and loss, and notes) deposited at the Mercantile Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Mercantil (Provincial Commercial Registry of the corporate seat)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a calendar-year entity: shareholders' approval within 6 months after 31 December (by 30 June) and deposit within 1 month after approval (by 31 July).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Registry closure ('cierre registral') preventing the registration of any public instruments until accounts are deposited; monetary fine under Ministry of Justice tariff of EUR 1,200–60,000 per year of delay depending on turnover; no automatic dissolution solely for late filing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual beneficial ownership declaration (Declaración de Titularidad Real) submitted together with the annual accounts
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Mercantil (attached to the annual accounts filing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Same deadline as the annual accounts deposit: within 1 month after approval of the annual accounts (e.g., by 31 July for a calendar-year entity).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines under Spanish AML law of up to EUR 10,000 for each false or incomplete beneficial ownership declaration; registry closure also applicable for failure to file annual accounts.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual third-party operations declaration (Modelo 347) for transactions exceeding EUR 3,000 per counterparty
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 1 February to 28 February (or the last business day of February) of the year following the reporting calendar year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of EUR 150 per operation (minimum EUR 438, maximum EUR 6,000); omissions may attract an additional penalty of EUR 175 per operation; no registry strike-off.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An independent audit is mandatory where the company meets at least two of the following three conditions for two consecutive fiscal years: total assets exceeding EUR 2,850,000, annual revenue exceeding EUR 5,700,000, or average headcount exceeding 50 employees.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Spanish GAAP per the Plan General de Contabilidad (PGC) for individual accounts; IFRS as endorsed by the EU for consolidated accounts of listed groups.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The annual accounts filing must include a signed identification of all ultimate beneficial owners (individuals holding more than 25% of capital, voting rights, or control). Any share transfer during the year must be reflected in the Register of Members and incorporated into the UBO declaration filed with the annual accounts. A negative declaration is required when no UBO exists.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Libro Registro de Socios)
Register of Corporate Resolutions / Minutes (Libro de Actas)
Register of Contracts with Directors, Shareholders, and Their Related Parties

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 400 – 1,200 per year for a professional registered address or corporate agent service in Spain
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,000 – 8,000 per year for a statutory or voluntary independent audit of an SL

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced 15% CIT rate for newly incorporated SLs in the first two profitable tax periods (Article 29.1 LIS). R&D and technological-innovation software credits (range 20-42% of qualifying expenses); digital gaming royalties qualify for partial deduction under the R&D-in-developing-software case law. No autonomous reduced rate for small turnover below EUR 1M; the general 25% rate applies.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_regime: Indefinite carryforward since 2015 (Article 26 LIS). No 5-year limit; offset is capped at 70% of the positive taxable base in each subsequent year, with lower caps (50%/25%) for groups with turnover above EUR 20M/60M and a EUR 1M minimum offset floor for large taxpayers.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 200 (Impuesto sobre Sociedades) filed via the AEAT electronic headquarters (Sede Electrónica), with mandatory digital certificate or Cl@ve PIN.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (Form 200) plus quarterly instalment prepayments on Form 202
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual return and final liquidation must be filed and paid within 6 months and 25 days after the end of the tax period. For a 31 December fiscal year-end, the deadline is 25 July of the following year. Quarterly instalments on Form 202 are due within the first 25 days of April, October and December (and the additional instalment in the first 20 days of July for entities with turnover exceeding EUR 600 million, or the ordinary April/October/December cycles for all).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Identification: NIF, corporate name, annual activity code (ISIC 5820 / CNAE 5821), net turnover and group membership.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Filed by the Spanish-resident SL itself; non-resident shareholders are not required to file Form 200 absent a Spanish permanent establishment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Fiscal year start and end dates, reduced-dimension entity indicators, and applicable special regime selections.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The entity remains a resident taxpayer; the SL's ownership by non-residents does not alter the declaration period or taxpayer status.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corrections to accounting profit for permanent and temporary differences, including non-deductible expenses, exemption-eligible income and transfer-pricing adjustments under Article 18 LIS.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Intra-group transactions with non-resident related parties (IP royalties, marketing fees, app-store user acquisition commissions) must be adjusted to arm's-length value.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Positive taxable base after application of prior-year NOL compensation (cap of 70% of the positive base per year for standard taxpayers).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: IAP/Google Play revenue must be fully accrued and invoiced; un-invoiced virtual-currency proceeds cannot be treated as deferred income solely for shareholder tax planning.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax computed at 25% (or 15% under the new-entity regime), before application of tax credits, deductions and double-taxation relief.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Credits applied must be supported by documentation; foreign-source dividends destined for repatriation are reconciled in this section.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total tax payable after deducting Form 202 instalments, withholdings and the quota paid abroad.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Dividend withholding at 19% (or 0% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary authorisation) must be reconciled with the payer's Form 200 settlement and Form 210/Ex-142 filings.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers the extemporaneous surcharge under Article 27 LGT: 5% (up to 3 months late), 10% (3-6 months), 15% (6-12 months), 20% (over 12 months), plus late-payment interest. Failure to file after formal notice attracts fixed penalties of EUR 200 to 6,000 per omission; underestimation penalties reach 50-100% of the tax under-assessed. Criminal prosecution applies when defrauded tax exceeds EUR 120,000.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: A non-resident shareholder must hold a certificate of fiscal residence (TRC) issued by the treaty jurisdiction and present it to the Spanish payer before the dividend payment date. The payer retains 19% unless the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive applies (EU/EEA corporate parent holding at least 5% for 12 consecutive months, filed via Form Ex-142 with proof of residence). Refunds of over-withheld amounts are obtained through an annual claim on Form 210 or under the special refund procedure, with the payer's Form 200 identifying the withholding in Box 90. Beneficial-ownership and substance evidence is mandatory; a letterbox parent without real activity is denied treaty and directive relief.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rates: 19.0% on interest and 19.0% on royalties paid to non-resident legal persons. Under the EU Interest-Royalties Directive (25% direct ownership, 2-year minimum holding) and applicable tax treaties, rates can be reduced to 0%; typical treaty lines reduce interest to 10-12% and royalties to 5-10%, conditioned on beneficial-ownership and anti-abuse clauses.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory full documentation (Local File and Master File) arises when annual net turnover reaches EUR 10,000,000. Below that threshold, Spanish law still requires simplified documentation for related-party transactions exceeding EUR 250,000 per operation or homogeneous group, and for transactions exceeding EUR 100,000 in aggregate with a single related party. Intragroup services, IP licensing, game-development fees and user-acquisition cost allocations are squarely within these thresholds.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Spain does not maintain an autonomous Economic Substance Regulation of the UAE-ESR type. Substance is nevertheless enforced through the general anti-abuse clause (Article 15 LGT), simulated-entity recharacterisation (Article 16 LGT), CFC rules (Article 100 LIS) and the judicial business-purpose doctrine. DAC6 (reportable cross-border arrangements) further requires disclosure of schemes lacking economic substance. Social-casino and virtual-gaming groups must demonstrate real employees, servers, development activity and management decisions in Spanish territory to sustain tax residence, treaty access and the 0% EU dividend rate.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Omitting Spanish-source digital gaming and IAP/Google Play revenues, or artificially shifting profits to a zero-tax offshore subsidiary through inflated royalties, underpaying corporation tax by an amount exceeding EUR 120,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 305 of the Criminal Code, fines ranging from double to six times the defrauded amount plus loss of subsidies and public procurement eligibility. The AEAT attaches non-criminal penalties of 50-100% of the under-assessed tax under Articles 184-197 LGT, with the evasion penalty imposed cumulatively.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who order, consent to or fail to prevent the evasion face imprisonment of two to six years, disqualification from receiving subsidies and from contracting with the public sector for up to ten years, travel bans via preventive registration, and extradition cooperation. Civil liability for the evaded quota and delays is jointly and severally attributed to management where corporate assets are insufficient.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the Spanish SL as a letterbox without employees, servers, management premises or actual decision-making, while the entire IP stream and gaming margin accrues in no-tax or low-tax affiliates and the Spanish entity invoices only a minimal margin.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterisation under Articles 15-16 LGT (GAAR and simulated contract) with a 50% penalty surcharge on the generated tax base; denial of treaty benefits under BEPS Action 6; CFC attribution of passive income under Article 100 LIS; refusal of the 0% EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive exemption.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Management can be held jointly and severally liable under Article 42 LGT for the hidden tax, with criminal exposure under Articles 310 and 305 Criminal Code for arrangements whose sole purpose is circumvention. Travel restrictions and director bans are available where the sham entity is used to launder gaming proceeds.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to prepare the Local File, Master File or simplified documentation; applying profit splits or marketing-user acquisition fees to related parties that yield margins outside the arm's-length range; or providing unsubstantiated benchmark studies for in-app purchase service arrangements.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article 18.13 LIS imposes a fine of 1% of the audited related-party transaction volume, subject to a minimum of EUR 1,000, for each missing or inaccurate documentation obligation. If recharacterisation is declared, the taxable base is increased by the full price differential plus a second-layer penalty of up to 50% of the additionally assessed tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The officer certifying the transfer-pricing documentation as correct is personally liable for proof concerning that certification; directors who knowingly approve intragroup pricing outside the arm's-length range are jointly liable for the resulting assessment. Non-resident directors may be reached through seizure of their Spanish assets, prohibitions on acquiring Spanish subsidies, and in egregious cases, travel bans under validation of the Economic and Administrative Courts.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Processing virtual currency and in-app purchases for simulated casino slots without robust AML/KYC controls; permitting anonymous, untraceable virtual-currency withdrawals; commingling user deposits with operational funds; or running an unlicensed gambling platform that substitutes actual casino play.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Ley 10/2010 AML sanctions escalate from EUR 60,001-150,000 for serious omissions to EUR 150,000-1,500,000 or 5% of gross turnover for very serious breaches, with additional AEAT audit risk for enforced collection of undeclared proceeds. Payment rails (Apple IAP, Google Play Billing) may be suspended and banking de-risking follows any suspicious-activity reports.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally liable for failing to adopt AML/KYC procedures, for signing off on unusual transactions without reporting, and for laundering proceeds deriving from tax evasion. Criminal exposure under Article 301 Criminal Code provides sentences of two to five years, travel bans through international arrest warrants, civil restitution to the tax authority, and veil-piercing by AEAT where the corporate form is used as a facade.
